advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] In scenario 1, capture the inbound pass's stderr and assert it has no `outbound_update` line for `key` with `releases` > 0, so an echo write is actually detected
evidence: `# An inbound release is not echoed back: Jira still holds exactly the one version.` followed by `assert _jira_versions(dc_transport, key) == [name]`
`_pass(dc_store_copy_repo, local_id, key, "inbound pass")` — the returned stderr is thrown away, so the pass's own record of what it wrote is never checked

src/rebar/reconciler/outbound_mutation_builders.py:321-329 prints `RECON: outbound_update key=... releases={len(release_mutations)}` for every update. That line is the only signal that can tell an echo write from no write, which is the reasoning `_assert_one_release_item`'s docstring already gives.

src/rebar/reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/_issues.py:199-202 `add_fix_version` sends the per-item `{"add": {"name": name}}` update. Adding a version that is already present leaves the end state unchanged.
advisory.finding: Scenario 1's 'not echoed back' check cannot fail if an echo happens. If the pass re-added the version it just imported, Jira's add is a no-op on a version the issue already holds, so `fixVersions` would still read `[name]`. The comment claims a guarantee the assertion does not test.
scenarios: A regression makes the inbound pass also plan an outbound add for the release it just imported. Jira's end state stays `[name]`, so scenario 1 still passes.
advisory.suggested_fix: Assign `stderr = _pass(...)` and assert that no `_UPDATE_LINE` match for `key` has a non-zero `releases=` group, e.g. `assert all(int(m.group(3)) == 0 for m in _UPDATE_LINE.finditer(stderr) if m.group(1) == key)`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the outbound add/remove scenarios check per-item writes using Jira's end state: put a Jira-only version on the issue before the pass and assert it is still there afterwards.
evidence: src/rebar/reconciler/outbound_mutation_builders.py:321-329 prints `RECON: outbound_update key=... changed=[{','.join(sorted(fields))}] ... releases={len(release_mutations)}` while planning, before `mutations.append(OutboundMutation(...))`. No write has happened yet.
search for `release` in src/rebar/reconciler/outbound_field_diff.py (where compute_update_fields lives) returned no matches, so `changed` can never contain `fixVersions`.
Test docstring: "a whole-list write would show ``fixVersions`` in ``changed``" / assertion `assert "fixVersions" not in changed`.

The actual per-item write happens later, in src/rebar/reconciler/dispatch_one.py:566-594 (`client.add_fix_version` / `client.remove_fix_version`) and src/rebar/reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/_issues.py:221-223 (`issue.update(update={"fixVersions": [item]})`). The stderr line cannot see either.

_issues.py:200-201 states the contract: per-item `update` 'so a concurrent Jira-side version edit is not clobbered'. No scenario adds a Jira-side version that rebar never held, which is the only end state that could distinguish a per-item write from a whole-field replace.

Test code: `_pass(dc_store_copy_repo, local_id, key, "inbound pass")` (return value discarded), followed by `# An inbound release is not echoed back: Jira still holds exactly the one version.` / `assert _jira_versions(dc_transport, key) == [name]`.

Inverted trace: if the outbound differ planned `{"action": "add", "release": name}` for this key, dispatch_one.py:583-584 would call `client.add_fix_version(issue_key, name)` on an issue that already has `name`. The REST read-back would still return `[name]`, so the assertion would still pass.
The same module already parses the pass's planned release count (`_UPDATE_LINE` ... `releases=(\d+)`), so an echo is observable in stderr.
advisory.finding: `_assert_one_release_item` claims to prove that fix versions were written one item at a time, but its source is the `RECON: outbound_update` line, which the planner prints before any write happens. `changed=` lists only the fields from `compute_update_fields`, and that function never produces `fixVersions`, so `"fixVersions" not in changed` can never fail. A regression in the write path (dispatch_one / the DC adapter) that switched to replacing the whole `fixVersions` field with rebar's full set would still print `changed=[] ... releases=1` and pass. The end-state checks would also pass, because rebar holds the full set.
merged_from: Scenario 1's check that the inbound release is not echoed back to Jira cannot detect an echo. A bad outbound `add` of a version the issue already has leaves Jira's end state unchanged, so `_jira_versions(...) == [name]` passes whether or not an echo happened. The pass's stderr, which could show it, is thrown away.
scenarios: Someone changes `_update_fix_versions` or `_update_one_dispatch_releases` to send `fields={"fixVersions": [<full intended set>]}`. The planner line still reads `changed=[] ... releases=1`, Jira's end state still equals rebar's set, and both outbound tests stay green.
advisory.suggested_fix: In scenario 2 (and 3), create a third version `foreign` and attach it with `dc_transport.add_fix_version(key, foreign)` after the search wait and before the second pass, so the pass's snapshot does not see it. Then assert `_jira_versions(dc_transport, key) == sorted([first, second, foreign])`. A whole-field replace from rebar's intended set would drop `foreign`. Keep the stderr check only as a plan-count check, or drop the `fixVersions not in changed` assertion, which can never fail.
